title.purpose: Detail panel sentence title ("Updated query"); balanced wrap.

section-title.purpose: Panel section headings: Changes, Context, Error, Recorded arguments.

body-small.purpose: Meta lines, notes, filter chips, card descriptions.

caption.purpose: Before / After captions and secondary lines (email under a name).

mono.purpose: Only machine-written text: code, ids, action names, IPs, recorded values.

shadows.name: focus-ring

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Background, border, colour and box-shadow changes on buttons, tabs and inputs.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: Disclosure chevron rotating 90deg; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: skeleton-shimmer
motion.purpose: Loading skeleton bars; static under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Panel insets tighten to 16px; label/value grids stack; Action filter goes full width.

knownLimitations: At 390px the global app header and main sidebar make every page wider than the viewport (788px with the sidebar open, 592px collapsed). App-shell limitation, out of scope; not a rule.

narrative.overview:
Weaver is an operator's console. Its surfaces read like a well-kept ledger: white or near-white sheets on a cool grey desk, divided by single hairline rules, with ink in three strengths (default, muted, soft). Nothing is framed that a rule can separate, and nothing is coloured that does not need to be acted on or judged. The one loud colour, Weaver red, belongs to the things you can do and the thing you are looking at; green and red status inks belong to outcomes. Everything else is greyscale and type weight.

Density is deliberate. Body copy runs at 13px, metadata at 12.5px, captions and identifiers at 12px, and hierarchy comes from weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 650) and ink strength rather than size jumps. Monospace is reserved for what a machine wrote: code, ids, actions, IP addresses and recorded values. The system ships light and dark themes from the same token names (`html[data-theme]`); every rule below holds in both.

The audit event panel is the clearest expression of the world: a right-side sheet that opens on a plain sentence ("Updated query"), puts the field-by-field change first, and keeps the who/when/outcome on one quiet meta line.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey desk (canvas-subtle) under white sheets (canvas-default), separated by 1px border-default rules.
One accent, Weaver red, for actions and current focus only.
Status colour only on outcomes and errors.
Hierarchy by weight and ink strength at small, dense sizes.
Flat surfaces; depth by tone and hairlines, with soft shadows held for floating layers.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Weaver red marks what you can do or what you are looking at (a button, a link-action, the open row, the focused field). It never decorates a heading, a section or a container.

rules.name: The Outcome Ink Rule
rules.body: Green and red status inks appear only on outcomes and errors, as a 7px dot beside a plain word ("Success", "Failed") or inside the error box. Status is never conveyed by colour alone.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Rank by weight before size: 650 for titles and section headings, 600 for emphasised values ("After", chip values, names), 500 for a field name that heads its own block, 400 for everything else. A field name must never match the weight of the section title above it.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace only for code, identifiers, action names and recorded values; never for labels, headings or prose (a description shows in the UI face even inside a code-style frame).

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate with a single 1px border-default rule before reaching for a frame; separate with a frame before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do use the token names (`var(--color-*)`) rather than literal hex, so both themes hold.
Do separate rows with a single 1px border-default rule and let the values carry the weight.
Do rank text with the weight ladder (650 / 600 / 500 / 400) at 13px and below before adding size.
Do pair every status colour with a word: a 7px dot plus "Success" or "Failed".
Do show secrets only as a hidden-value chip ("Changed (hidden)"); name JDBC property keys, never their values.
Do give every custom interactive element the shared focus ring and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do collapse label/value grids to one column below 600px.
donts: Don't use Weaver red on headings, section titles, borders of passive containers or decoration.
Don't use green or red status inks for anything but outcomes and errors.
Don't set labels, headings or prose in monospace.
Don't add shadows to cards, chips or inline boxes; flat surfaces with hairlines are the default.
Don't let a field name match the 650 weight of its section title.
